One domain change can break a full table.

SAP domain, Part 11 of 12: the key points.

1. One domain serves many data elements, and every field that uses them
2. Change the domain (e.g. length 10 to 12) and all of them change
3. A table that already holds data is adjusted with SE14 (database utility)
4. Programs never TYPE a variable with a domain, always with the data element
5. INT4 = whole numbers, FLTP = floating point (never for money)

slides.heading: Interview *round 1*

messages.text: STANDARD, SORTED or HASHED: which one for big lookups?
HASHED. A read by the full unique key takes the same time at any size.

slides.voiceover: Which one for big lookups? Hashed. A read by its full unique key stays fast at any size.
slides.spoken: Which one for big lookups? Hashed. A read by its full unique key stays fast at any size.

slides.label: ALL THREE
slides.heading: Know *all three*
slides.title: Internal table types
slides.voiceover: Standard reads by index, fine for small tables. Sorted keeps its key in order, so partial key reads are fast. Hashed needs the full unique key.
slides.spoken: Standard reads by index, fine for small tables. Sorted keeps its key in order, so partial key reads are fast. Hashed needs the full unique key.

slides.label: THE TRAP
slides.heading: Reading by a *partial key*
slides.voiceover: The trap: read a hashed table with a partial key, and it searches row by row. For partial keys, pick sorted.
slides.spoken: The trap: read a hashed table with a partial key, and it searches row by row. For partial keys, pick sorted.

posts.caption:
STANDARD, SORTED or HASHED? It comes up in almost every SAP ABAP interview.

An internal table is a table in memory inside your program.

1. STANDARD: index access, linear search by key. Fine for small tables and ALV output
2. SORTED: kept sorted by its key, binary search, fast partial key reads
3. HASHED: full unique key only, the same read time at any size
4. Trap: a partial key on a HASHED table means a slow row-by-row search

Comment HASHED if you'd have got this one right.

SAP domain, Part 12 of 12: mistakes and interview questions.

slides.label: THE PROBLEM
slides.heading: A domain has *no name*
slides.voiceover: A domain only gives a type and a length. It has no name and no meaning. A data element adds the field labels and the meaning.
slides.spoken: A domain only gives a type and a length. It has no name and no meaning. A data element adds the field labels and the meaning.

slides.heading: Two *layers*
steps: Table field: uses the data element
slides.voiceover: Think of two layers. The domain is the shape: char, length one. The data element is the meaning: order status. Table fields use the data element.

slides.body: It sits on a domain and gives the field its business meaning and its screen labels.
